abstract.text: We argue that BPS ansatzes, entering manifestly vacuum BPS monopole solutions to equations of motion in the (Minkowskian) non-Abelian Higgs model play the role of some electric form-factors and that this implies (soft) violating the CP-invariance of the mentioned model, similar to taking place in the Euclidian Yang-Mills (YM) theory with instantons, generating the θ-term in the appropriate effective Hamiltonian.

evidence.quote: Historically, the idea to go over to the limit (1.4) in the YMH model is originated from the works [6], and from this time it was refer to as the Bogomol’nyi-Prasad-Sommerfeld (BPS) limit.

predecessors.why: The paper builds on the BPS limit and Prasad-Sommerfeld monopole solutions.

evidence.quote: there can be drawn a highly transparent parallel between the Minkowskian YMH vacuum involving vacuum BPS monopole solutions and a liquid helium II specimen described in the Bogolubov-Landau model [17].

predecessors.why: The superfluid analogy is built on the Bogolubov-Landau model of liquid helium II.

evidence.quote: The starting point of our discussion will be the well known Dirac quantization condition [27] for the electric and magnetic charges presented in a closed system of quantum fields.

predecessors.why: The analysis starts from Dirac’s electric-magnetic charge quantization condition.

evidence.quote: In this section, repeating the arguments [30], we shall attempt to demonstrate that the presence of YM BPS ansatz f 1 BP S, (1.8), in the (Minkowskian) YMH BPS monopole theory violates manifestly the CP invariance of that theory.

replications.why: The CP-violation argument explicitly repeats Witten’s treatment of dyon charge quantization.

evidence.quote: The just described superfluidity is absent in another Minkowskian Higgs models with monopoles: for instance, in the ’t Hooft-Polyakov model [22, 23].

targets.why: The paper contrasts its BPS monopole vacuum with the ’t Hooft-Polyakov model, where electric form-factors become trivial.

evidence.quote: It is the effect similar to that taking place in the instanton models [1, 2, 8, 25], generating the θ-items in the appropriate effective Lagrangians.

targets.why: The instanton θ-term is used as the closest similar CP-violating mechanism, though BPS case has no θ-dependence.

evidence.quote: The principal goal of the present note is to show that BPS ansatzes f 1 BP S (r), f 0 BP S (r), one encounter in the Higgs BPS monopole model, can serve as electric form-factors therein.

thesis.text: BPS ansatzes in the Minkowskian non-Abelian Higgs model act as electric form-factors and thereby induce soft CP violation, analogous to the instanton θ-term but without a θ-angle.
